bio_en: Artashes Vanarian (born Hatsagortsian) was born in the Norashen quarter of Aygestan, Van, in 1892 and studied at the Yeramian school and from 1909 at the Van Central school. He graduated in law from the University of Constantinople in 1914 and later worked in America as a lively speaker and writer, publishing a volume of articles against Bolshevism. He died at Niagara Falls on 9 July after complications of an appendix operation and was buried in Detroit; his bequest bought the building of the ARF museum at Montmorency, opened in 1936.
